data.name: home.lead
data.value: Check mail security, DNS and networks right in the browser. No account, no server, input stays local.

data.name: home.privacy
data.value: Only the mail domain check and DNS diff send DNS queries to Cloudflare DNS (fallback Google Public DNS). Everything else runs offline.

data.name: privacy.dns
data.value: The mail domain check and DNS diff query DNS records via DNS over HTTPS at Cloudflare (cloudflare-dns.com), or at Google (dns.google) if Cloudflare fails. Only the queried names and types are transmitted, plus the device's IP address for technical reasons.

data.name: privacy.hosting
data.value: The static files are served via Cloudflare Pages. Cloudflare processes connection data required for delivery.

data.name: privacy.local
data.value: Language, color scheme and the history of the mail domain check and subnet calculator are kept in the browser's localStorage. Headers, passwords, tokens and certificates are never stored. The history can be cleared in the tools.

data.name: privacy.p1
data.value: This app has no server component, no accounts and no tracking. All calculations run in the browser.

data.name: tool.diff.desc
data.value: Zone file from before against live DNS. Ideal for DNS migrations.

data.name: tool.header.desc
data.value: Route as a timeline, SPF/DKIM/DMARC results, spam hints and suspicious mismatches.

data.name: tool.helpers.desc
data.value: Passwords, JWT, Base64/URL/hex, hashes and certificates. Works offline.

data.name: tool.mail.desc
data.value: MX, SPF with lookup count, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI, MTA-STS and TLS-RPT with traffic lights and suggestions.

data.name: tool.subnet.desc
data.value: IPv4 and IPv6, splitting, summarizing and IP-in-network check.

data.name: home.why.1
data.value: As an IT administrator, the same questions come up every week: Why does our mail end up in spam? Are SPF, DKIM and DMARC right? Did a record go missing after the DNS move? Does the subnet still fit?

data.name: home.why.2
data.value: Since February 2024, Google and Yahoo require bulk senders to have valid SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, and Microsoft has enforced the same for Outlook.com since May 2025. If a record is missing, mail is rejected or lands in spam. Small companies notice it too, as soon as newsletters or invoices sent by mail stop arriving.

data.name: home.why.3
data.value: The usual online checkers show ads, want an account or send mail headers with internal addresses to third-party servers. This toolbox does all the work in the browser. Only DNS lookups go to Cloudflare DNS, just like with any resolver.

data.name: home.rules.spf
data.value: Lists the servers allowed to send for the domain. At most 10 DNS lookups.

data.name: home.rules.dkim
data.value: Signs every mail so changes on the way are noticed. Keys with at least 1024, better 2048 bits.

data.name: home.rules.dmarc
data.value: Tells receivers what to do when SPF and DKIM fail, and sends reports. Start with p=none, then tighten.

data.name: home.rules.note
data.value: Google and Yahoo require this from around 5,000 mails a day to their users, Microsoft for Outlook.com. Sources:

data.name: home.guide.1
data.value: Run the mail domain check for the sending domain. Red and yellow findings come with a concrete suggestion for the DNS record.

data.name: home.guide.2
data.value: Copy the headers (Outlook: File, Properties; Gmail: Show original) and paste them into the header analysis. It shows the route, delays and whether the sender is faked.

data.name: home.guide.3
data.value: Export the zone file at the old provider before the move. Afterwards the DNS diff compares it with live DNS and lists every missing record.

data.name: home.guide.4
data.value: Enter a network in the subnet calculator, split it into VLANs or check whether an address belongs to it. IPv4 and IPv6.

data.name: home.tech
data.value: C# and .NET 10 compiled to WebAssembly (Blazor). No backend: the app is served as static files from Cloudflare Pages.

data.name: home.tech.link
data.value: Source code and tests on GitHub
